raw_text:
# 12-Week Strength Programme
## Client Profile & Programming Rationale

**Client:** Female, 47, advanced lifter, early perimenopause
**Start date:** 1 June 2026
**Primary goals:** Bone density preservation and enhancement, lean muscle maintenance, long-term metabolic health
**Medical clearance:** Full resistance training approved by GP
**Key constraints:** No sauna or heat-based recovery modalities; no fasted high-intensity work in heated environments; structured post-session cooling protocol mandatory after all high-intensity sessions

---

### A Note on Perimenopause and This Programme

Oestrogen decline in perimenopause accelerates bone resorption, reduces muscle protein synthesis efficiency, and impairs thermoregulation. The research base is clear: heavy compound loading — particularly axial loading through the spine and hip — is among the most potent non-pharmacological interventions for bone mineral density. This programme therefore keeps heavy barbell work central throughout all 12 weeks. Cycle irregularity means we cannot reliably phase training around a follicular/luteal model, so instead the programme uses a **load-undulation model** built around weekly and session-level variation rather than hormonal phase. On weeks where the client reports high fatigue, poor sleep from night sweats, or heat intolerance, a pre-planned deload substitution is available for each session (noted throughout).

---

## Structural Overview

| Phase | Weeks | Primary Stimulus | Rep Ranges | Intensity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 — Foundation & Technique Audit | 1–3 | Movement quality, connective tissue prep, baseline strength | 5–8 | 65–75% 1RM |
| Phase 2 — Hypertrophy-Strength Bridge | 4–6 | Muscle cross-section, bone loading volume | 4–8 | 72–82% 1RM |
| Phase 3 — Maximal Strength | 7–9 | Peak force production, bone strain stimulus | 2–5 | 82–92% 1RM |
| Phase 4 — Strength-Power Integration | 10–12 | Rate of force development, consolidation | 3–6 + power work | 78–88% 1RM + low-load explosive |

---

## Session Structure (All Phases)

**Training frequency:** 4 sessions per week
**Session labels:** A (Lower — Hip Dominant), B (Upper — Push/Pull), C (Lower — Knee Dominant), D (Upper — Horizontal/Vertical Integration)
**Recommended weekly layout:** Monday A / Tuesday B / Thursday C / Friday or Saturday D — with Wednesday and Sunday as full rest or active recovery. This layout is flexible; the key is that no two lower-body sessions fall on consecutive days.

**Standard session architecture:**
1. **Thermal warm-up (10 min):** Room-temperature environment. Light cardio (rowing, cycling) at low intensity — not to raise core temperature aggressively, but to mobilise joints and increase tissue pliability. Fan or air conditioning running throughout.
2. **Mobility & activation (8–10 min):** Hip 90/90s, thoracic rotation, glute activation, shoulder CARs.
3. **Main work (35–50 min):** Compound primary lifts first, accessory work second.
4. **Accessory & corrective work (10–15 min):** Targeted single-joint or stability work.
5. **Structured cooling protocol (10–15 min, mandatory after Sessions A and C, recommended after B and D):** See cooling protocol section below.

---

## Structured Cooling Protocol

This is non-negotiable after all lower-body sessions and any session rated RPE 7 or above. It is a direct medical accommodation for heat intolerance and vasomotor symptoms.

**Protocol:**
- Cease main work and move immediately to a cool (ideally air-conditioned or fan-cooled) space.
- Apply cold water to pulse points: wrists, inner elbows, back of neck, temples. A damp cool towel kept in a cooler bag is practical.
- Consume 400–500 ml of cold water (4–8°C if tolerated) over 10 minutes.
- Perform 5 minutes of diaphragmatic breathing (4 counts in, 6 counts out) in a seated or supine position — this activates the parasympathetic nervous system and assists thermoregulation.
- Remain in the cool environment for a minimum of 10 minutes post-session before showering.
- Shower in cool-to-lukewarm water, not hot.
- Log any hot flash occurrence, intensity (1–5), and duration in the training log. This data will inform session timing and environment adjustments.

**Session environment:** Wherever possible, train in air-conditioned spaces. If training outdoors or in a non-climate-controlled gym during summer months (this programme begins June 2026), schedule sessions before 9 am or after 6 pm to avoid peak ambient heat. Avoid training in direct sunlight.

---

## Deload Substitution Rule

On any week where the client reports three or more of the following — poor sleep for 3+ consecutive nights, hot flash frequency above her personal baseline, significant fatigue, mood disruption, or joint tenderness — the planned session is replaced by its deload variant. Deload variants are listed for each phase. This is not failure; it is intelligent periodisation for a fluctuating hormonal environment.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation and Technique Audit (Weeks 1–3)

**Dates:** 1 June – 21 June 2026

**Phase rationale:** Even for an advanced lifter, a 3-week foundation phase serves critical purposes here. It establishes baseline strength numbers for percentage-based loading in later phases, audits movement quality under moderate load (perimenopause can alter joint laxity and proprioception), and begins bone loading at a volume the connective tissue can absorb before intensity climbs. Sets are kept to 3–4 working sets. Rest periods are 2–3 minutes for compound work, 60–90 seconds for accessories.

---

### Week 1 (1–7 June 2026)

**Theme:** Establish baselines, reinforce movement patterns, introduce loading.

**Session A — Lower Body, Hip Dominant**

*Warm-up:* 8 minutes easy rowing, hip 90/90 mobility (2 × 60 seconds each side), banded clamshells (2 × 15).

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Back Squat** — 4 sets × 6 reps @ 65% estimated 1RM. This is the primary bone-loading exercise for the lumbar spine and hip. Axial loading through the spine is the key stimulus. Full depth, controlled 3-second eccentric. Rest 3 minutes between sets. Note: if the gym is warm, reduce to 3 sets and prioritise cooling.
- **Romanian Deadlift** — 3 sets × 8 reps @ 60% 1RM. Hip hinge pattern, hamstring and glute loading, secondary spinal loading. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- **Hip Thrust (barbell)** — 3 sets × 10 reps @ moderate load. Glute and posterior chain development, hip extension strength. Rest 2 minutes.
- **Walking Lunges** — 3 sets × 10 reps each leg, bodyweight or light dumbbells. Unilateral loading, balance, hip stability.

*Accessory:*
- Copenhagen Plank — 3 × 20 seconds each side (adductor and hip stability, important for hip bone density).
- Single-leg Glute Bridge — 2 × 15 each side.

*Cooling protocol:* Full protocol as described above.

---

**Session B — Upper Body, Push/Pull**

*Warm-up:* 8 minutes light cycling, shoulder CARs (2 × 5 each direction), band pull-aparts (2 × 15), thoracic rotation (2 × 8 each side).

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Bench Press** — 4 sets × 6 reps @ 65% 1RM. Upper body pressing, pectoral and anterior shoulder loading. Rest 3 minutes. Note: bench press provides compressive loading through the wrist, elbow, and shoulder — relevant for upper limb bone density.
- **Barbell Bent-Over Row** — 4 sets × 6 reps @ 65% 1RM. Horizontal pull, upper back, rear deltoid, biceps. Spinal erector isometric loading. Rest 3 minutes.
- **Overhead Press (barbell or dumbbell)** — 3 sets × 8 reps @ 60% 1RM. Axial loading through the shoulder girdle, important for proximal humerus and clavicular bone stress. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- **Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-Up** — 3 sets × 8 reps. Vertical pull pattern.

*Accessory:*
- Face Pulls — 3 × 15 (rotator cuff health, shoulder longevity).
- Dumbbell Lateral Raise — 3 × 12.
- Tricep Pushdown — 2 × 15.

*Cooling protocol:* Recommended but not mandatory unless RPE ≥ 7.

---

**Session C — Lower Body, Knee Dominant**

*Warm-up:* 8 minutes easy bike, quad foam roll, ankle mobility (2 × 10 circles each), glute activation (banded squats 2 × 15).

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Front Squat** — 4 sets × 5 reps @ 62% 1RM. Greater quadriceps demand than back squat, upright torso reduces spinal shear while maintaining axial load. Rest 3 minutes. If front squat is not in the client's repertoire, substitute goblet squat with heavy dumbbell for this phase only.
- **Bulgarian Split Squat (rear foot elevated)** — 3 sets × 8 reps each leg, moderate dumbbell load. Unilateral knee-dominant loading, hip flexor stretch, balance. Rest 2 minutes per leg.
- **Leg Press** — 3 sets × 10 reps @ moderate-to-heavy load. High-force knee extension, secondary bone loading through femur. Rest 2 minutes.
- **Nordic Hamstring Curl or Lying Leg Curl** — 3 sets × 8 reps. Hamstring eccentric strength, knee joint health.

*Accessory:*
- Step-Up with Knee Drive (dumbbell) — 3 × 10 each leg.
- Terminal Knee Extension (band) — 2 × 20 each leg (VMO activation, knee stability).

*Cooling protocol:* Full protocol mandatory.

---

**Session D — Upper Body, Horizontal/Vertical Integration**

*Warm-up:* As Session B.

*Main work:*
- **Incline Dumbbell Press** — 4 sets × 8 reps. Upper pectoral and anterior deltoid emphasis.
- **Barbell or Dumbbell Row (chest-supported or Pendlay)** — 4 sets × 8 reps. Horizontal pull variation.
- **Pull-Up or Weighted Pull-Up** — 3 sets × 5–6 reps (add load if bodyweight is easy). Vertical pull, lat and bicep loading, shoulder girdle bone stress.
- **Arnold Press** — 3 sets × 10 reps. Shoulder stability and strength through full range.

*Accessory:*
- Cable Row (single arm) — 3 × 12 each side.
- Dumbbell Curl — 3 × 12.
- Band External Rotation — 2 × 15 each side.

*Cooling protocol:* Recommended.

---

### Week 2 (8–14 June 2026)

**Theme:** Increase load modestly (+2.5–5 kg on main lifts where form was solid in Week 1). Begin tracking RPE per set.

The session structure remains identical to Week 1. The following adjustments apply:

- **Back Squat:** Increase to 67–68% 1RM. Add a 5th set if Week 1 felt manageable and recovery was good.
- **Romanian Deadlift:** Increase by 2.5–5 kg.
- **Bench Press and Row:** Increase by 2.5 kg if technique was clean.
- **Front Squat:** Maintain Week 1 load and focus on depth and bar position before adding weight.
- **Overhead Press:** Increase by 2.5 kg.
- **Pull-Up:** If weighted, add 2.5 kg.

**Additional Week 2 note:** Begin logging hot flash frequency and sleep quality in the training diary this week. Use a simple 1–5 scale for sleep quality and a tally for hot flash frequency. This data will be reviewed at the end of Phase 1 to calibrate Phase 2 loading.

---

### Week 3 (15–21 June 2026)

**Theme:** Final baseline week. Attempt a conservative working-max test on Back Squat and Deadlift (not a true 1RM — a 3RM performed at high effort, from which 1RM can be estimated). This gives accurate percentages for Phase 2.

**3RM Testing Protocol (Session A, Week 3):**
- Extended warm-up: 10 minutes, plus 3 progressively heavier warm-up sets before the working sets.
- Back Squat: Work up to a 3RM over 4–5 sets. Rest 4 minutes between heavy sets. Record load.
- Romanian Deadlift: Work up to a 5RM (not 3RM — to protect the lower back on the same day as squats). Record load.
- Reduce accessory volume this session to 2 exercises only.

**3RM Testing Protocol (Session C, Week 3):**
- Front Squat: Work up to a 3RM or heavy 5RM.
- Leg Press: Work up to a 10RM.

**Session B and D, Week 3:**
- Bench Press: Work up to a 3RM.
- Overhead Press: Work up to a 5RM.
- Pull-Up: Work up to a 3RM (weighted if applicable).
- Row: Work up to a 5RM.

**1RM Estimation Formula:** Use the Epley formula — Load × (1 + Reps/30) — to calculate estimated 1RM from the 3RM or 5RM results. These numbers become the basis for all Phase 2 and Phase 3 percentage prescriptions.

**Phase 1 Deload Variant (use any week if needed):**
Replace all barbell work with dumbbell equivalents at 50–55% of estimated 1RM. Reduce sets to 3. Keep all accessory work. Maintain the cooling protocol. This is not a rest week — it is a reduced-load week that still provides bone stimulus.

---

## Phase 2: Hypertrophy-Strength Bridge (Weeks 4–6)

**Dates:** 22 June – 12 July 2026

**Phase rationale:** This phase bridges hypertrophy-range work (which builds muscle cross-section and contributes to bone loading through muscular pull on bone) with the heavier strength work coming in Phase 3. Loads increase to 72–82% 1RM. Volume is at its highest point in the programme. Sets increase to 4–5 working sets on primary lifts. Rest periods are 2.5–3.5 minutes for compound work. This is the phase most likely to generate heat during sessions — environmental management is critical.

**Summer heat note:** By late June, ambient temperatures in many UK and European locations will be at their highest. Confirm gym air conditioning is functional. If the client trains at home or in a non-climate-controlled space, shift all sessions to early morning (before 8 am) or evening (after 7 pm). Cold water bottle in a cooler bag is mandatory kit.

---

### Week 4 (22–28 June 2026)

**Session A — Lower Body, Hip Dominant**

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Back Squat** — 5 sets × 5 reps @ 75% 1RM. This is the primary bone-loading stimulus of the programme. Five sets of five at this intensity generates significant compressive force through the lumbar vertebrae and femoral neck — the two sites most vulnerable to osteoporotic fracture. Rest 3.5 minutes.
- **Conventional Deadlift** — 4 sets × 5 reps @ 75% 1RM. Replaces Romanian Deadlift as the primary hinge this phase. Full deadlift provides greater axial spinal loading. Rest 3.5 minutes.
- **Hip Thrust (barbell)** — 4 sets × 8 reps, heavy. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- **Reverse Hyper or Back Extension** — 3 sets × 12 reps. Posterior chain, spinal erector endurance.

*Accessory:*
- Copenhagen Plank — 3 × 25 seconds each side.
- Pallof Press — 3 × 12 each side (anti-rotation core stability).

*Cooling protocol:* Full protocol mandatory.

---

**Session B — Upper Body, Push/Pull**

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Bench Press** — 5 sets × 5 reps @ 75% 1RM. Rest 3.5 minutes.
- **Barbell Bent-Over Row** — 5 sets × 5 reps @ 75% 1RM. Rest 3.5 minutes.
- **Overhead Press** — 4 sets × 6 reps @ 72% 1RM. Rest 3 minutes.
- **Weighted Pull-Up** — 4 sets × 5 reps. Rest 3 minutes.

*Accessory:*
- Face Pulls — 3 × 15.
- Dumbbell Lateral Raise — 3 × 12.
- Hammer Curl — 3 × 12.
- Tricep Dip or Pushdown — 3 × 12.

---

**Session C — Lower Body, Knee Dominant**

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Front Squat** — 4 sets × 5 reps @ 73% 1RM. Rest 3.5 minutes.
- **Bulgarian Split Squat** — 4 sets × 6 reps each leg, heavy dumbbell or barbell. Rest 2.5 minutes per leg.
- **Leg Press** — 4 sets × 8 reps, heavy. Rest 2.5 minutes.
- **Romanian Deadlift** — 3 sets × 10 reps @ 65% 1RM. Moved here as a secondary accessory lift this phase.

*Accessory:*
- Step-Up with Load — 3 × 10 each leg.
- Nordic Hamstring Curl — 3 × 6 (eccentric focus, 4-second lowering).

*Cooling protocol:* Full protocol mandatory.

---

**Session D — Upper Body, Integration**

*Main work:*
- **Incline Barbell Press** — 4 sets × 6 reps @ 73% 1RM. Rest 3 minutes.
- **Pendlay Row** — 4 sets × 5 reps @ 75% 1RM. Rest 3 minutes.
- **Weighted Pull-Up** — 4 sets × 5 reps. Rest 3 minutes.
- **Dumbbell Shoulder Press** — 3 sets × 8 reps.

*Accessory:*
- Cable Row — 3 × 12.
- Dumbbell Curl — 3 × 12.
- Rear Delt Fly — 3 × 15.

### Week 5 (29 June – 5 July 2026)

**Theme:** Load progression. Increase all primary lifts by 2.5–5 kg where Week 4 sets were completed at RPE 7–8. If any set reached RPE 9–10, maintain the same load. Volume remains the same.

**Specific adjustments:**
- Back Squat: +2.5–5 kg.
- Deadlift: +5 kg (deadlift tolerates slightly larger jumps).
- Bench Press: +2.5 kg.
- Row: +2.5–5 kg.
- Overhead Press: +2.5 kg.
- Front Squat: +2.5 kg.
- Pull-Up: +2.5 kg added load.

**Week 5 additional note:** Introduce **contrast loading** in Session A this week. After the final set of Back Squat, perform 3 × 3 Box Jumps (low box, 30–40 cm) with 2 minutes rest. The heavy squat pre-activates the neuromuscular system, and the subsequent explosive movement generates high-rate bone strain — a distinct and additive stimulus to slow heavy loading. This is a brief introduction before it becomes a formal programme component in Phase 4.

### Week 6 (6–12 July 2026)

**Theme:** Deload week within Phase 2. This is a planned, mandatory deload — not optional. After two weeks of high-volume loading, a reduction in volume (not necessarily intensity) allows connective tissue recovery and hormonal system recovery. For a perimenopausal client, this deload is particularly important as cortisol management is more challenging with declining oestrogen.

**Week 6 deload structure:**
- Reduce sets on all primary lifts from 5 to 3.
- Maintain load (do not reduce weight — this preserves the neural adaptations).
- Reduce accessory work to 2 exercises per session.
- Maintain all four sessions.
- Maintain cooling protocol.
- Prioritise sleep and nutrition this week (see nutrition section).

**Session A (deload):**
- Back Squat — 3 × 5 @ 75% 1RM.
- Deadlift — 3 × 5 @ 75% 1RM.
- Hip Thrust — 2 × 10.
- Copenhagen Plank — 2 × 20 seconds.

**Session B (deload):**
- Bench Press — 3 × 5 @ 75% 1RM.
- Row — 3 × 5 @ 75% 1RM.
- Pull-Up — 2 × 5.
- Face Pulls — 2 × 15.

**Session C (deload):**
- Front Squat — 3 × 5 @ 73% 1RM.
- Bulgarian Split Squat — 2 × 6 each leg.
- Nordic Curl — 2 × 5.

**Session D (deload):**
- Incline Press — 3 × 5.
- Pendlay Row — 3 × 5.
- Pull-Up — 2 × 5.
- Rear Delt Fly — 2 × 15.

## Phase 3: Maximal Strength (Weeks 7–9)

**Dates:** 13 July – 2 August 2026

**Phase rationale:** This is the highest-intensity phase of the programme. Loads reach 82–92% 1RM. Volume decreases relative to Phase 2 (fewer total sets, fewer reps per set), but the mechanical load on bone is at its peak. Research by Kerr, Beck, and colleagues consistently shows that high-magnitude loads — even at low volumes — are the most potent stimulus for bone mineral density improvement. Sets are 3–4 working sets. Reps are 2–5. Rest periods extend to 4–5 minutes between heavy sets to allow full neuromuscular recovery.

**Heat management in Phase 3:** Shorter rep sets mean less metabolic heat generated per set, but the intensity of effort is high. The cooling protocol remains mandatory. Sessions may feel shorter in duration but should not feel easier — the nervous system demand is significant.

### Week 7 (13–19 July 2026)

**Session A — Lower Body, Hip Dominant**

*Main work:*
- **Barbell Back Squat** — 4 sets × 4 reps @ 82% 1RM. Rest 4 minutes. This is the cornerstone of the bone-loading programme. At 82% 1RM, ground reaction forces and spinal compressive forces are substantially above the threshold required to stimulate osteoblast activity.
